content.text: {"concept_key":"c8-english-subject-verb-agreement","title":"Subject-Verb Agreement","quick":"The verb must match the subject. Singular subjects like 'he/she/it' take verbs with 's' or 'es' in simple present tense.","full":"Think of a kirana shop: one shopkeeper 'sells' sweets, but two shopkeepers 'sell' sweets. Singular subject (she, he, it, one person) needs the verb with 's/es' added in simple present tense. Plural subjects (they, we, I) use the plain verb form. Here 'She' is singular, so 'go' becomes 'goes'.","traps":["Writing 'go' instead of 'goes' with she/he/it","Adding 's' to verbs with plural subjects like 'they go'","Confusing present tense form with past tense (went)"],"misconception":"Child thinks the verb form only depends on the action word, not on whether the subject is singular or plural.","parent_questions":[{"q":"If I say 'He ___ (play) cricket', what word goes in the blank?","expected_answer_hint":"plays - because 'he' is singular"},{"q":"Why can't we use 'go' with 'she'?","expected_answer_hint":"Because 'she' is singular, needs 's/es' added to verb"}],"check_question":{"q":"Fill: He ___ (eat) rice every day.","options":["eats","eat","ate"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! 'He' is singular, so verb takes 's'.","wrong_feedback":"Not quite. 'He' is singular, so the verb needs 's' added: eats."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A schoolgirl walking happily toward her school gate in the morning with a bag on her back.","labels":[{"text":"She","position":"top-left"},{"text":"goes","position":"top-right"},{"text":"school","position":"bottom"}]}}
